summary: git merge combines the commits from another branch into the current branch. Switch to the branch that should receive the changes first.
notes: A fast-forward happens when the current branch has no new commits. Git moves the branch name forward and makes no merge commit.
A merge commit has two parents. In the graph, it is where two lines join.
--no-edit accepts the default merge message instead of opening an editor.
pitfall: Merging while on the wrong branch merges in the wrong direction. Run git branch or git status before git merge.
setup_note: Starts on main with two commits. Two branches start from main: letter-grades (a change to gradebook.py) and readme-typo (a fix to README.md).
setup:
cat > gradebook.py <<'EOF'
scores = [88, 92, 79, 95]
average = sum(scores) / len(scores)
print("Average:", average)
EOF

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Gradebook
Quiz socres for Period 3.
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add gradebook script"

cat > scores.csv <<'EOF'
name,score
Ava,88
Liam,92
Noah,79
Zoe,95
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add quiz scores"
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Print a letter grade"
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Fix typo in README"
